question.problem:
Which of the following statements regarding quadratic forms are true?

I. $R(x)=8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$ is positive-definite

II. $S(x)={x}^{T}\,[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}]x$ is negative-definite

III. $T(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}$ is indefinite
question.worked_solution:
Recall that, a quadratic form $Q(x)$ is:

- positive-definite if $Q(x)>0$ for all $x\in {R}^{n}∖\{0\};$

- negative-definite if $Q(x)<0$ for all $x\in {R}^{n}∖\{0\};$

- indefinite if 

- $Q({x}_{1})>0$ for some ${x}_{1}\in {R}^{n},$ and

- $Q({x}_{2})<0$ for some ${x}_{2}\in {R}^{n}.$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the quadratic forms in turn.

- Statement I is false. Substituting ${x}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}R({x}_{1}) & =8\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\  & =8>0,\end{aligned}
$$

while substituting ${x}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R({x}_{2}) & =8\cdot 1\cdot (-1) \\  & =-8<0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the quadratic form is indefinite.

- Statement II is true. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-2{x}_{1}^{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-(2{x}_{1}^{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2})<0\end{aligned}
$$

for all $x\in {R}^{n}∖\{0\}.$ So, the quadratic form is negative-definite.

- Statement III is false. Indeed, since

$$
\begin{aligned}T(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}>0\end{aligned}
$$

for all $x\in {R}^{n}∖\{0\},$ the quadratic form is positive-definite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
